introduction_markdown: You are required to answer FIVE questions, choosing THREE from Section A and TWO from Section B. All the questions carry equal marks and marks allocated to parts of questions are indicated. Extra questions answered from each section shall NOT be marked. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Duration: two and a half hours.
incertitudes: Le PDF a 3 pages (page de garde, Section A, Section B), rien ne manque. Scan avec filigranes, ignores.
Choix : la page de garde impose 5 questions, 3 parmi la Section A (questions 1 a 5) et 2 parmi la Section B (questions 6 a 9). Traduit en regles_choix : SECTION A 3 sur 5, SECTION B 2 sur 4.
Points imprimes par sous-partie recopies tels quels : 7(c) imprime (3,3,2marks) soit 8 points (6+6+8 = 20) ; 1(b) imprime 10 marks ; 6(b) (2,2,2,2,2) = 10 ; 9(a) (6,6,6) = 18 et 9(b) 2.

Aucun corrige officiel : tous les corriges sont rediges. Les schemas demandes au candidat (cellule animale, oeil, nephron) sont decrits dans le corrige, sans figure. Le sujet ne contient aucune figure.

questions.enonce_markdown: How does the excessive consumption of alcohol affects the society? *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Excessive consumption of alcohol harms society in these ways (any six points):

1. **Accidents**: drunk drivers cause many **road accidents**, injuries and deaths; accidents also occur at work.
2. **Crime and violence**: drunkenness leads to **fighting, rape, theft, murder** and other crimes, and to a breakdown of law and order.
3. **Family problems**: money is spent on alcohol instead of food, school fees and health care, causing **poverty, child neglect, domestic violence, quarrels and divorce**.
4. **Poor productivity**: absence from work, loss of concentration and **loss of jobs** reduce output and the economy of the country.
5. **Health costs**: alcohol causes **liver cirrhosis, ulcers, heart and brain damage and addiction (alcoholism)**; the cost of treatment is a burden on families and on the state.
6. **Moral decay**: it spoils the **reputation** of the drinker and encourages **school drop-out, prostitution** and early pregnancies among the young.

questions.enonce_markdown: How can excessive consumption of alcohol be combated? *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Excessive drinking of alcohol can be combated by (any six points):

1. **Education and sensitisation** of the public (in schools, churches, media) on the dangers of alcohol.
2. **Laws**: banning the **sale of alcohol to minors** (below 18 years), restricting **opening hours** and the number of bars, and banning drunk driving, with **checks and fines**.
3. **Heavy taxation** and higher prices of alcoholic drinks, and **control of advertising**.
4. **Counselling and rehabilitation** of alcoholics by medical personnel and support groups such as Alcoholics Anonymous.
5. **Parental control and good examples** from parents and elders at home.
6. **Providing leisure activities** (sports, clubs, youth centres) and **employment** for young people so that they have an alternative to drinking.

questions.enonce_markdown:
How can the following parts of the body be taken care of?

(i) hands

(ii) the eye

(iii) the ear. *(3,3,2marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Hands**: **wash them with soap and clean water** before eating and preparing food and after using the toilet; **keep the nails short and clean**; wear **gloves** for dangerous work; **treat cuts and wounds** at once with antiseptic; avoid handling sharp or hot objects without protection.

(ii) **The eye**: **do not rub** it with dirty hands or cloths; **read in good light** and avoid very bright light (wear dark glasses); keep **sharp objects, chemicals and dust** away or wear goggles; eat a diet rich in **vitamin A**; **have regular eye tests** and wear the prescribed glasses; wash an infected eye with clean water and seek treatment.

(iii) **The ear**: **do not push sharp objects (pins, matches)** into the ear; **remove wax gently** or have it removed by a doctor; **avoid very loud noise** (loud music) or wear ear protection; **treat ear infections** promptly; keep the ear dry and clean, and do not hit or pull it.
